claim: NEXLOAD overwrites 0x5B00-0x5BFF before the game starts, so a snapshot that keeps code, stack or data there starts wrong unless the build restores the whole 256 bytes.
limit: A read of 5B5C alone did not matter in Atom Ant or Ruff and Reddy (real loader showed 0x10 there in every mode); check what the game does with the byte.

evidence.text: Temporary NEXLOAD5B00-5BFF workspace restored completely, not only the start-up tail.
evidence.quote: Temporary NEXLOAD5B00-5BFF workspace is restored completely.

evidence.text: Code lives at 5B00-5BEE (entry 5B00); NEXLOAD writes that buffer, so a set-up call in the stub bank copies 5B00-5BFF back.
evidence.quote: The game keeps code at 5B00-5BEE (entry at 5B00). NEXLOAD writes that buffer, so it must come back.

evidence.text: Stack at 0x5B76, inside the buffer NEXLOAD overwrites, returning into ROM paging code at 0x5BB0; found by scanning every published patch with nexload=True.
evidence.quote: the snapshot's stack is at 0x5B76, in the printer buffer NEXLOAD overwrites, and its top

evidence.text: The game reads 5B5C (its 7FFD copy) and NEXLOAD overwrites the printer buffer; keep_printer_buffer is 48K only, so setup restores it.
evidence.quote: NEXLOAD overwrites the printer buffer and the game reads 5B5C (its 7FFD copy).

evidence.text: The game reads 0x5B00 before writing it and NEXLOAD overwrote it, so the snapshot's printer buffer is put back.
evidence.quote: snapshot's printer buffer put back (the game reads 0x5B00 before writing it; NEXLOAD overwrote it).
